open_points.subject: public_op:store.read_records error contract
open_points.text: Relations section: "A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation names or passes one of another kind"; but operation section: "Errors: `unknown_reference` for the whole call when any named identity does not exist"
open_points.question: When `store.read_records` is called with a malformed relation argument set (wrong/missing/extra args), must it return `internal_error`, or is `unknown_reference` the only allowed error?
options: Return `internal_error` for malformed relation arguments, `unknown_reference` only for missing named records
open_points.default_guess: Return `internal_error` for malformed relation arguments, because the Relations section states this explicitly.

open_points.subject: MCP get_repair_view continuation-token validation ownership
open_points.text: `get_repair_view` says its continuation token "also carries the implementation set of its first page" and is "bound to its slot"; conventions also say "surface checks the token's form; whether it names a position of that list is answered by `store.page_records`"
open_points.question: Which module must validate the extra `get_repair_view` token bindings (slot id and frozen implementation set), and at what step relative to `store.page_records` token-position validation?
options: `surface` validates slot+implementation-set binding before calling `store.page_records`; `store` validates only list position
`store.page_records` validates both position and these higher-level bindings
open_points.default_guess: `surface` validates slot and implementation-set binding before `store.page_records`, which should only validate position for the supplied record type/filter.
